supply.heading: Skills that hold up on camera

items.title: Aerialists
items.body: Silks, hoop, straps, rope and trapeze — performers who work at height to a rigger's brief and repeat the move take after take.

items.title: Acrobats & tumblers
items.body: Hand-to-hand, tumbling, banquine and group acrobatics, from single moves in shot to full ensemble sequences.

items.title: Skill and object work
items.body: Contortion, balance, juggling, cyr wheel, unicycle, fire and object manipulation — genuine skill, performed to camera.

items.title: Creature & physical performers
items.body: Movement-trained performers for suit, puppetry, mask and creature work, comfortable in costume for a full shoot day.

approach.heading: Trained performers, not a novelty booking
approach.body: Circus reads badly on camera when it is cast on the strength of a showreel alone. We put forward performers whose training and current practice match the specific skill in the brief, we are clear about what needs rigging, matting or a qualified rigger present, and we flag it early if what has been storyboarded is not safely repeatable. If a sequence needs a specialist alongside the performer, we will say so rather than let it land on the day.

points.description: The specific discipline in the brief checked against current training and practice, not a general circus credit.
Rigging, height, matting and floor requirements raised at brief stage so the location can actually take it.
Cast for performers who can hold the move across takes and coverage, not land it once.

approach.pullQuote: “If it cannot be repeated safely on take nine, it is not a shot — it is a stunt with a different name.”
